title: Persist router lifecycle transitions to the canonical board
description:
## Problem

The live router run for KBS-c11aec preserved a Codex session, raw transcript, checkpoint, branch, and draft PR, and emitted `open -> in_progress -> review` state-transition events on the shared router-state branch. The canonical issue JSON remained `open`, however. `kbs router recover` then attempted an invalid direct `open -> review` transition, leaving the board unable to show the reviewable work without manual reconciliation.

## Required behavior

Every router lifecycle transition must be atomically reflected in canonical Kanbus issue state through the configured lifecycle path, as well as in the durable router event stream. A completed run must visibly land in Review; an agent question or launcher fault must visibly land in Blocked. Recovery must be idempotent and must never attempt an invalid shortcut transition.

## Acceptance criteria

- Python and Rust persist `Open -> In Progress -> Review` (or `Blocked`) to the canonical issue.
- Router state, board state, and console/API responses converge after a restart or Git refresh.
- `router recover` is idempotent and respects configured lifecycle transitions.
- A completed live or scripted Codex turn always has a visible summary/comment, draft PR, and the configured board status.
- Regression coverage exercises the KBS-c11aec event sequence and Git-only refresh path.
